title: Free LPA Form 1 applications for Singapore Citizens and LPA uptake figures
asked: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked for the number and percentage of Singaporeans over 65 who have registered an LPA, how that compares with overall adult uptake, and whether the Ministry had finished considering extending the LPA Form 1 fee waiver beyond 31 March 2026.
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming said MSF will make LPA Form 1 applications free for all Singapore Citizens even after the current fee waiver ends. As of 20 February 2026, 404,000 Singapore Citizens, about one in seven, had made an LPA; among those above 65, 197,000, about one in four, had done so. He said uptake has been healthy with the OPG Online portal and legacy planning campaigns, but many still have not made an LPA, and encouraged Singaporeans to do so while fit and healthy.

key_points.point: LPA Form 1 applications will be free for all Singapore Citizens even after the current fee waiver ends.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we will make Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) Form 1 applications free of charge for all Singapore Citizens, even after the current fee waiver ends.

key_points.point: As of 20 February 2026, 404,000 Singapore Citizens, or about one in seven, have made an LPA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: As of 20 February 2026, 404,000 or about one in seven Singapore Citizens have made an LPA.

key_points.point: Among Singaporeans above 65, 197,000, or about one in four, have made an LPA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Amongst those aged above 65 years old, 197,000 or about one in four have done so.

key_points.point: The launch of the Office of the Public Guardian Online portal and island-wide legacy planning campaigns contributed to healthy LPA uptake.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: with the launch of the Office of the Public Guardian Online portal and more visible legacy planning campaigns island-wide, we have seen a healthy uptake of LPA applications.

key_points.point: Many Singaporeans still have not made an LPA, and the Ministry wants to continue urging them to do so.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we want to continue to urge Singaporeans to make their LPA.

key_points.point: Having an LPA gives peace of mind by naming someone trusted with legal authority to decide when one no longer can.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Having an LPA in place will allow Singaporeans and our loved ones to have peace of mind

left_open: A comparison with overall adult LPA uptake, as distinct from the overall Singapore Citizen figure.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered public education and language support for LPA, and difficulties with the Office of the Public Guardian website.
